statements.quote: He will never be anything but a sexual predator in the minds of the community
statements.context: About the author's former high-school advisor ('Mr. D'), convicted of possessing and sharing child pornography and now in jail. The author predicts the community will always regard him as a sexual predator. The same sentence continues 'although he will be released from prison in a few years' (logged separately).
statements.note: Prediction about a private individual's reputation; compound sentence split into two statements.

statements.quote: he will be released from prison in a few years
statements.context: Same sentence about the author's former advisor Mr. D, convicted of child pornography offenses; the author expects his release from prison within a few years of the post (dated 2024-02-22).
statements.note: Compound sentence split; about a private individual, low forecast value.

statements.quote: I can only imagine the rate of adult male humans who will book a chemical castration follow-up with a PCP is likely to be low.
statements.context: Discussing chemical castration (Lupron and similar medicines) as a treatment for pedophilic urges, after citing Korean law and recidivism data. The author expects voluntary uptake of chemical castration through primary care to be low among men who have not offended.
statements.note: Hedged uptake prediction about general behavior; no date.

statements.quote: Perhaps it will be a plausible way to reduce risk.
statements.context: The author cites data that GLP-1 medicines such as semaglutide (Ozempic) reduce cravings beyond food, notes trials underway in alcohol and nicotine use disorders, and says his patients report fewer sexual cravings. 'It' = GLP-1 medication as a way to reduce child sexual abuse risk in people with pedophilic urges. Preceded by 'This will be an open question.' and followed by 'People could request the treatment without having to scream, I am a pedophile.'
statements.note: Speculative; hedged with 'Perhaps'. Concerns a possible future clinical use, not a trial readout.

statements.quote: Neurofeedback guided by fMRI might also be a plausible option.
statements.context: After noting that FDA-cleared TMS variants for smoking cessation target regions that line up with imaging findings in child sexual abuse perpetrators, the author suggests fMRI-guided neurofeedback as another possible brain-targeted intervention for pedophilic urges.
statements.note: Speculative treatment possibility; borderline forward-looking.

statements.quote: I know they're going to throw it into the fire
statements.context: Gollum-voice parody about the psychiatry EHR Luminello after its acquisition by SimplePractice, which was taken private by private equity the prior month. 'It' = Luminello; the author states the acquirer is going to shut Luminello down (title: Specialty Psychiatry EHR Luminello Shuts Down; also 'They are shutting down our precious Luminello!'). Embedded in the rhetorical question 'Why would I sign up for Luminello now when...'.
statements.note: Lord of the Rings parody framing; the underlying claim (Luminello will be shut down) reads as sincere.

statements.quote: They won't, precious! Gollum.
statements.context: Answer to the author's own questions 'What about my controlled substances precious? How will my patients get them?' He notes SimplePractice has no ePrescribing solution yet, so once Luminello is gone his patients will not get controlled-substance prescriptions through the acquirer's platform.
statements.note: Parody voice, hyperbolic. Underlying claim: SimplePractice will lack controlled-substance ePrescribing for former Luminello users.

statements.quote: They would destroy it. They would throw it in the fire.
statements.context: 'They' = the private equity owners of SimplePractice and Luminello; 'it' = the author's practice's medical records ('our precious medical records'). The author claims private equity does not care about the records and would destroy them.
statements.note: Parody voice; hyperbolic conditional about medical records. Restated as 'they will burn us, with our records' (logged separately).

statements.quote: they will burn Ken, and they will burn us, with our records
statements.context: Ken = the psychiatrist founder of Luminello. The author predicts that private equity, driven by liquidation preferences, will harm the founder and the clinician users along with their medical records after the SimplePractice acquisition.
statements.note: Parody voice; restatement of the records claim, adds an outcome for the founder.

statements.quote: Business models built on this impracticality won’t work either.
statements.context: Essay prompted by Greenbrook TMS being delisted from a stock exchange. 'This impracticality' = traditional TMS requiring 36 once-daily visits because insurers pay once a day, which depressed patients with pathological indecision cannot manage. The author predicts business models built on 36-day TMS will not work.
statements.note: General prediction about TMS clinic business models; the author is founder of Fermata, a competing interventional psychiatry practice.

statements.quote: Well, of course , that wasn’t going to change.
statements.context: Reacting to UnitedHealth Group's SEC 8-K on the February 21, 2024 Change Healthcare cyberattack, which said the company had not determined the incident was reasonably likely to materially impact its financial condition or results of operations. The author, sarcastically, agrees: UHG's financial condition will not be materially hurt.
statements.note: Sarcastic tone but reads as a real expectation; endorses UHG's own filing language as the obvious outcome.

statements.quote: in what I imagine will be the only way to get 6TB of PHI to not be a catastrophic HIPAA-fine disaster
statements.context: The author's own framing sentence before a satirical press release imagining Optum acquiring the BlackCat ransomware group ('Why not just acquire the breach?'). Implies that the Change Healthcare breach of about 6TB of protected health information will otherwise be a catastrophic HIPAA-fine disaster for UnitedHealth Group.
statements.note: Implicit forecast of catastrophic HIPAA fines; the press-release body is fiction and was not logged.

statements.quote: If I don't move fast enough, I lose access to my charts.
statements.context: The author requested export of his medical records from Luminello over a week earlier with no result, while being emailed to switch to acquirer SimplePractice. Conditional about losing access to his own patient charts if he does not migrate in time.
statements.note: Personal conditional about the author's own records access; low forecast value.

statements.quote: Your valuation will collapse, and there's nothing in it
statements.context: Line from the author's parody of the Pixies song 'Where Is My Mind', addressed to SimplePractice and Luminello over the failed medical-record export. Claims the company's valuation will collapse.
statements.note: Parody lyric; hyperbole that does not read as a real expectation. A later verse repeats 'Your stock will collapse' although SimplePractice is privately held.

statements.quote: Regulators will fill your day
statements.context: Parody lyric verse: 'Your stock will collapse, and Regulators will fill your day'. Directed at SimplePractice and Luminello for failing to export the author's medical records; the author expects regulatory trouble (compliance enforcement) over the record-access failure. The refrain says 'Way out of compliance, need enforcement'.
statements.note: Parody lyric, but the regulatory-trouble claim reads as a real expectation; the 'stock will collapse' half of the line is hyperbole (logged separately as sincere=false).

statements.quote: Way out of compliance— could be a class action!
statements.context: Parody lyric refrain about SimplePractice and Luminello's failure to return the author's charts; the author suggests the non-compliance could lead to a class action lawsuit.
statements.note: Hedged litigation possibility inside a parody lyric.

statements.quote: I'm not gonna sell out
statements.context: After receiving an email encouraging him to sell his business, the author states he will not sell out (to private equity). Full sentence: 'All I Gotta say is, that I'm not gonna sell out, the pixies are going on tour again this summer.'
statements.note: Own intention about the author's own business (likely Fermata); coder may mark CONTROL.

statements.quote: the pixies are going on tour again this summer
statements.context: Same sentence; the author states the Pixies will tour again in summer 2024 (post dated 2024-03-01), as a joke about not selling out.
statements.note: Restates a public tour announcement; trivial, low forecast value.

statements.quote: At some point, somebody is going to get subpoenaed about this, if they haven't been already, and they're gonna have to answer a lot of questions.
statements.context: About the Change Healthcare (UnitedHealthcare / Optum) cyberattack and data breach, after the author's TikTok explainer went viral. The author predicts subpoenas and questioning of those responsible; the question he wants answered is what Change Healthcare does.
statements.note: Compound: subpoena plus questioning; hedged by 'if they haven't been already'.

statements.quote: they make more money the longer this goes on, not less
statements.context: Open letter to the BlackCat ransomware hackers extorting UnitedHealth Group over Change Healthcare. The author argues UHG profits from the outage: premiums keep flowing in while claims payments are frozen, and UHG, which owns a bank, earns interest on about $730m every day it cannot pay claims.
statements.note: Present-tense incentive analysis with a forward implication (UHG gains as the outage continues); restated as 'They make more money every single day they can't pay out claims'.

statements.quote: United healthcare will survive if United healthcare has a delay in paying United healthcare.
statements.context: Explains that Change Healthcare is part of Optum, part of UHG, and that UHG pays itself (netted out under 'corporate and eliminations'). Conditional prediction that UnitedHealthcare survives a delay in internal payments caused by the cyberattack.
statements.note: Conditional, low-uncertainty claim.

statements.quote: UHC is gonna crush you like they do all the rest of us.
statements.context: Closing warning to the ransomware hackers: the author predicts UnitedHealthcare will prevail over them, as it does over providers and patients. Preceded by 'Their incentive is not to get this over with quickly.'
statements.note: Rhetorical open-letter framing; reads as a real expectation that UHC comes out ahead of the extortionists.

statements.quote: Now, it's probably the worst liability I can imagine when it comes to cyber security and a flood of incoming lawsuits.
statements.context: Opening of an illustrated tour of Optum's public Change Healthcare service-status page (created the evening of March 5, 2024). The author characterizes Change Healthcare as the worst cyber-security liability he can imagine and expects a flood of incoming lawsuits.
statements.note: Compound: liability characterization plus an expected flood of lawsuits (litigation).

statements.quote: It's just the beginning.
statements.context: Immediately after 'Oh my God, that looks like a lot of problems with information systems!' while walking through screenshots of the Change Healthcare service-status page. The phrase may mean more problems are coming, or may only introduce the rest of the page tour (next line: 'Let's start with what's going well').
statements.note: Ambiguous: may not be a forecast at all; logged for recall.

statements.quote: credentialing is going to slow down!
statements.context: Commenting on the status page section showing Change Healthcare's provider communications and credentialing services offline; the author predicts provider credentialing will slow down as a consequence of the outage.
statements.note: Operational consequence of the outage.

statements.quote: sort of kind of promise to keep dissecting drugs or making fun of myself
statements.context: Podcast post intro. The author half-promises to keep producing his usual newsletter content (drug analysis, self-mockery) alongside the Change Healthcare coverage; the post itself publishes a podcast recorded before UHC paid the ransom.
statements.note: Own-newsletter content intention; trivial. Coder may mark CONTROL.
